items.title: 68359_Zutty Singleton oral history interview
items.q: But what I'd like to say I had Edmund Hall was playing the clarinet too, we had a trio, see? So, old Hank would make the introduction in one key and then when he'd go to the chorus to start on the tune he'd change the key.

ctx.x: And so Zutty came home and told me, he said I fired Hank tonight. I'm sick of him getting drunk. We couldn't play at all tonight. So I said, you fired him? Did you give him two weeks notice? He said, I fired him.

But what I'd like to say I had Edmund Hall was playing the clarinet too, we had a trio, see? So, old Hank would make the introduction in one key and then when he'd go to the chorus to start on the tune he'd change the key. And old Hall would say, man, what's the matter with you? You see, he was trouble (?).
Well he was drunk most of the time. Really drunk all the time. But a good piano player.

items.title: Edmond Hall Interview, 1957-04-11
items.q: I think Zutty was drumming with him

ctx.x: Just a few doors from Canal Street? Yeah, that's right. Right in the middle of the block. Armstrong used to work there too? Yeah. Barney Big Garden. That's the first place I heard Armstrong. It was at Tom Anderson. At that time he was using a piano, drums, I think Zutty was drumming with him, and the trumpet. And every night when we'd come. Piano player? Huh? I don't know who was the piano player, Tom. Because that night when we'd come from gigging we had to, I don't know, we had to change, right here on Rampart…
Do you know Udell Wilson, did you ever know him? No. I think he's from Kansas City and he played around.
